The turbine blade was made of a single crystal nickel-based superalloy called DD6, which has a two-phase microstructure with coherent and cuboidal γ' precipitates in a γ matrix.
The TMF test rig was capable of applying cyclic thermal and mechanical loads with a trapezoidal stress/temperature waveform, with a stress ratio R=0.05.
The minimum and maximum temperatures in the thermal cycle were 200°C and 980°C, respectively.
The experiment was terminated after 325 cycles when a crack emerged at the suction side near the trailing edge.
No cracks were observed at the film-cooling holes or other locations on the specimen.
The researchers developed a novel sample preparation method involving wire electrical discharge machining and mechanical separation to preserve the crack surfaces for detailed inspection.
Fatigue striations were observed on the crack surfaces, indicating the crack propagated from the inside wall towards the outside.
The estimated crack propagation life was 64 cycles, which accounted for 19.7% of the total fatigue life.
The finite element simulation, using a viscoplastic constitutive model, predicted the maximum accumulated slip strain at the pin-fin fillet, validating the experimental findings.
The maximum accumulated slip strain at the pin-fin fillet was 54.8% higher than at the film-cooling holes, indicating the pin-fin fillet had the weakest TMF resistance.
The researchers recommended measures such as increasing the pin-fin fillet radius and lowering the temperature in that region to improve the TMF resistance of the turbine blade.
The high frequency induction heating system allowed for convenient control of the desired temperature field and provided a sufficiently high heating rate.
The load synchronizer maintained a stable phase shift between the thermal and mechanical loads by adjusting the heating/cooling signals based on the real-time temperature feedback.
The particularly designed specimen with a shroud at the tip provided adequate load-bearing capability to simulate the actual turbine blade loads in the laboratory.
The TMF test rig and specimen design proved to be reliable, as no failures occurred in the test rig during the experiment.
